questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Both the academic opportunities that I could receive there (being able to take more than just 2 or 3 classes) was deffinetly one of the reasons, but also the fact that I had already been in Korea before and had made so many friends that I wanted to go back and see them again.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: none

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy, as I had already spent a semester abroad on a mandatory exchange trip, and this was the second time I had gone through a similar experience.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had an orientation a few days before the semester started, giving us the chance to meet some of our co-students, but also some of the full-time students at the university, creating the opportunity for us to make friends a bit before the start of the semester, so that we were not completely alone

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: none

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it fairly easy, as I used the same platform I used last time (Enkostay) and chose a place that I found suitable for myself.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That rent might be higher than a dorm, and they have to be aware that they are responsible for making sure they have the correct documentation for proof of living, as they will need that for their ARC application and ALSO that they have to make sure they know where they will recive their phycical mail as they will need to pay for NHIS bill that comes every month, as well as transportation time to and from campus can take longer than they think.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: none

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: DO BE AWARE of the fact that registation it a first come first sever bacis and that registration usually opens at 10 am KST(Korean standard time), and there are often onlya  few spots for exchange students, and if you don't get a spot you'll need to e-mail the professor or come to the class to get a signiture for allowing you a spot in the class

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You get an email a few weeks in advans decribing the process of making a proiority list of classe you want to take and then a week or so before registation you will get an e-mail tell you how to register and how to sign up to the class, BUT everything will be explained in the e-mails you will recive from the University you are going to and AGAIN DO BE AWARE of the fact that registation it a first come first sever bacis and that registration usually opens at 10 am KST(Korean standard time) so make sure to set an alarm if you are not in korea or also do if you are, and there are often only a few spots for exchange students, and if you don't get a spot you'll need to e-mail the professor or come to the class to get a signiture for allowing you a spot in the class.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was always possible to contact the university's OIR office that handled international student affairs.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very successful and had to reevaluate what class I wanted or what was left over that I still found interesting, but ended up taking classes that I both wanted to participate in and also found myself enjoying and interesting.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you are quick on the computer and that you get up in good time to sign up for the classes that you want, BUT ALSO do have back-up classes that you 100% would want to take in place of the first/original ones.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: None

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some of the courses might seem like introductory levels, but they are not, and some others might be exactly that, and it is really a trial-and-error kind of situation, so it is hard to describe. Some classes might be on our gymnasium level, and some others, there might be this general understanding that you already should know some of it, even though it is and introdution level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Most of my classes were either online or a flipped-learning style, where for the online ones you only had tests/exams either in person or online, and online submitted asignmets and the classes in it self was pre-recoded vidoes you would have to watch before a certain deadline. For the flipped-learning style, it was somewhat of the same, where you would have videos you would have to watch before class/deadline, and then you show up to class and apply the information gained from the videos to that day's class, and then submit an assignment by the end of the week. So the teaching style wasvery diffrent from teacher to teacher, but all were very knowledgeable in their own field.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

All three of these class was absolutly wounderfull and so informative in their own way, and created a space for learning where you still wanted to learn more afterwards, but also classes that were good on introductory levels and were easy to keep up with.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Loved the buddy concept

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Trips and fun activities around the city with the buddy program, as well as food/dining out events, and a few parties

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Cultural/language exchanges are not necessarily only those on campus, but also some independent ones around the city

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go see other cities like Busan, Jeonju, Paju, etc., but also go to the tourist spots like Starfield Library, aquarium, museum, etc., as they are also very fun and interesting.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very, but I have also been there before and had a lot of friends there to help me if needed

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open and take the initiative, and attend as many student events as you want and can.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There is a whole lot of respecting others in diffrent way and forms, not just formally and officialy but also informally and unofficialy so keep in mind to be respectful and polite

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kindness and the helpfulness, but also the food and drinking culture is some very special and fun to explore.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be active in participating in the club events, as they are very fun
Be up-to-date with all information and news regarding classes and courses, and be outseeking of the information
Be open to be spontaniouts as the best experiences and activities might pop up randomly in a very short time spand

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If attending the Seoul Campus, be aware that it is a VERY uphill walk, and the long wait for getting into the elevators therefor account for the longer walk or make sure to take a bus or two earlier than you think you need cuase it sucks to be late for class with all the walking and stairs.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the trips, new friends, adventures, new experiences, and knowledge that I was able to gain.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Staying open and active, as living alone can create a feeling of loneliness and a downward feeling, and make it a struggle to get up and out if you don't have any plans.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: None

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
